title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 73-74
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 73 to 74 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 73 to 74 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 73 to 74.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 73 to 74** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः । पूर्णः पूरयिता पुण्यः पुण्यकीर्तिरनामयः ॥** **मनोजवस्तीर्थकरो वसुरेता वसुप्रदः । वसुप्रदो वासुदेवो वसुर्वसुमना हविः ॥**

He is worthy of praise and loves to be praised; the hymn, the praise and the one who praises is he. He who loves the battle is that God of gods. Full, the fulfiller, holy, of holy fame, free of all illness. Swift as the mind, the maker of sacred fords, the giver of wealth is he. Vasudeva, the treasure, the good mind and the offering is that God of gods.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 73 to 74 mean?
faq.a: He is worthy of praise and loves to be praised; the hymn, the praise and the one who praises is he. He who loves the battle is that God of gods. Full, the fulfiller, holy, of holy fame, free of all illness. Swift as the mind, the maker of sacred fords, the giver of wealth is he. Vasudeva, the treasure, the good mind and the offering is that God of gods.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
